evidence: Announcement header: "Posted on 2025-09-25 by PostgreSQL Global Development Group"; body: "The PostgreSQL Global Development Group today announced the release of PostgreSQL 18"

claim: Before 18 Postgres relied on OS readahead and waited for each I/O to finish in sequence
evidence: Verbatim: "PostgreSQL previously relied on operating system readahead mechanisms to accelerate data retrieval." and "AIO lets PostgreSQL issue multiple I/O requests concurrently instead of waiting for each to finish in sequence."

claim: The OS cannot anticipate database access patterns, so readahead is suboptimal
evidence: Verbatim: "because operating systems lack insight into database-specific access patterns, they cannot always anticipate what data will be required, leading to suboptimal performance in many workloads"

claim: AIO in 18 covers sequential scans, bitmap heap scans and vacuum
evidence: Verbatim: "AIO operations supported in PostgreSQL 18 include sequential scans, bitmap heap scans, and vacuum." Release notes E.6.3.1.3 say the same ("sequential scans, bitmap heap scans, vacuums, etc.")

claim: PostgreSQL 18 adds an asynchronous I/O subsystem; backends queue multiple read requests
evidence: Release notes E.6.3.1.3: "Add an asynchronous I/O subsystem (Andres Freund, Thomas Munro, Nazir Bilal Yavuz, Melanie Plageman) ... This feature allows backends to queue multiple read requests"

claim: io_method selects the AIO method; values are worker, io_uring and sync
evidence: Docs: "Selects the method for executing asynchronous I/O. Possible values are: worker ... io_uring (requires a build with --with-liburing / -Dliburing) ... sync (execute asynchronous-eligible I/O synchronously)"

claim: io_method can only be set at server start
evidence: Verbatim: "This parameter can only be set at server start."
Verbatim: "The default is worker." On-screen `SHOW io_method;` output `worker` is this documented default printed in psql's standard SHOW layout; not captured from a live server

claim: The default number of I/O worker processes is 3
evidence: Verbatim: "Selects the number of I/O worker processes to use. The default is 3." On-screen `SHOW io_workers;` output `3` is this documented default; not captured from a live server

claim: The new I/O subsystem has shown up to 3x faster reads from storage in benchmarks
evidence: Verbatim: "a new I/O subsystem that has demonstrated up to 3x performance improvements when reading from storage" and "Benchmarking has demonstrated performance gains of up to 3x in certain scenarios." Shown on screen as "up to" and "in benchmarks"

claim: effective_io_concurrency and maintenance_io_concurrency defaults were raised to 16
evidence: Release notes: "Increase server variables effective_io_concurrency's and maintenance_io_concurrency's default values to 16 (Melanie Plageman)"

claim: pg_aios system view lists in-use AIO handles
evidence: Verbatim: "The pg_aios view lists all Asynchronous I/O handles that are currently in-use." Not used on screen
Source says "up to 3x" "in certain scenarios" for reads from storage only. Do not generalise
